title: Chapter 29. Nagari Padas — III: the cycle of the *Bhakti-ratnakara* (Yadunandana, Narahari Chakravarti) and the "Narahari" padas of GPT (sect. 3.2, nos. 39–45, 86–93)
html:
On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27; on the two poets named Narahari (Narahari Sarakara and Narahari Chakravarti) and on the attribution labels ("probably Sarakara", "probably Chakravarti", "not established"), see the introductory note to the "Narahari" appendix in chapter 17.

1. Yadunandana — "gaurāṅga carita āju ki pekhalum̐ māi…" (BR 12, pp. 904–905; GPT1 p. 167, no. 34)

Nagari-bhava. A woman of Nadia tells what she saw on the road: crying "Radha, Radha!", Gauranga weeps, embracing Gadai, rolls on the ground, streams flow from His eyes; she herself loses all composure; Dasa Gadadhara smiles softly. Raga dhanashi.1

গৌরাঙ্গ চরিত আজু কি পেখলুঁ মাই ।
রাধা রাধা বলি কান্দে ধরিয়া গদাই ॥

gaurāṅga carita āju ki pekhalum̐ māi |
rādhā rādhā bali kānde dhariyā gadāi ||

gaurāṅga carita — Gauranga's doings; āju — today; ki pekhalum̐ — what have I seen; māi — O mother (exclamation); rādhā rādhā bali — crying "Radha, Radha"; kānde — He weeps; dhariyā gadāi — embracing Gadai

1.1What have I seen today, mother — what Gauranga does!
Crying "Radha, Radha!" He weeps, embracing Gadai.2

ধরিতে না পারে হিয়া ধরণী লোটায় ।
ধূলা লাগিয়াছে কত ও না হেম-গায় ॥

dharite nā pāre hiyā dharaṇī loṭāya |
dhūlā lāgiyāche kata o nā hema-gāya ||

dharite nā pāre hiyā — cannot hold His heart; dharaṇī loṭāya — rolls on the ground; dhūlā lāgiyāche — dust has clung; kata — how much; o nā hema-gāya — to that golden body

1.2Unable to hold His heart, He rolls on the earth —
how much dust has clung to that golden body!

সে মুখ চাহিতে হিয়া কি না জানি করে ।
কত সুরধুনী-ধারা আঁখি বহি পড়ে ॥

se mukha cāhite hiyā ki nā jāni kare |
kata suradhunī-dhārā ām̐khi bahi paṛe ||

se mukha cāhite — looking at that face; hiyā — the heart; ki nā jāni kare — I do not know what it does; kata suradhunī-dhārā — how many streams like the Suradhuni; ām̐khi bahi paṛe — pour from His eyes

1.3I look at that face — and do not know what my heart is doing;
how many streams, like the Suradhuni, pour from His eyes!3

মৈলুঁ মৈলুঁ কেন গেলুঁ সে পথ বাহিয়া ।
ধৈরয না ধরে চিতে ফাটি যায় হিয়া ॥

mailum̐ mailum̐ kena gelum̐ se patha bāhiyā |
dhairaya nā dhare cite phāṭi yāya hiyā ||

mailum̐ mailum̐ — I am dying, dying; kena gelum̐ — why did I go; se patha bāhiyā — along that road; dhairaya nā dhare cite — there is no steadiness in my mind; phāṭi yāya hiyā — my heart bursts

1.4I am dying, dying! Why did I go along that road!
There is no steadiness in my mind, my heart is bursting.

দেখি দাস গদাধর লহু লহু হাসে ।
এ যদুনন্দন কহে ওই রসে ভাসে ॥

dekhi dāsa gadādhara lahu lahu hāse |
e yadunandana kahe oi rase bhāse ||

dekhi — seeing; dāsa gadādhara — Dasa Gadadhara; lahu lahu hāse — smiles softly, softly; e yadunandana kahe — Yadunandana says; oi rase bhāse — floats in that rasa

1.5Seeing this, Dasa Gadadhara smiles softly, softly.
Yadunandana says: he floats in that rasa.4

Chakravarti, describing the places of Navadvipa, says that the Lord lingered by this tree and then went along the bank of the Ganga, "and here women full of anuraga (anurāgabatī) joyfully and softly spoke with one another" — and gives their words in songs, "the first in a song of Sri Yadunandana Chakravarti, disciple of Sri Dasa Gadadhara Thakura" (so in BR). Eleven more songs follow in BR (nos. 2–7 of this chapter; Narahari's padas "nadīyāra mājhāre nācaye gorācām̐da" and "sai kibā aparūpa rūpa", translated in chapter 17; Yadunandana's pada "dekha dekha gorācānde" — chapter 11, no. 12; Vasu's PK 2149 — chapter 27, no. 7; Devakinandana's pada "nadīyāra mājhāre onā rūpa" — the poet is outside the corpus). GPT1 — p. 167, no. 34 (dhanashi; scan PDF p. 426); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 34 (catalogue: YN-002). Yadunandana Chakravarti was a disciple of Gadadhara Dasa, a poet of the late 16th century; his padas in BR are B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). of Krishna, calls Radha and embraces Gadadhara Pandita: according to the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (147–153), Gadadhara is Radha Herself; cf. chapter 11 (nos. 12–14) and Yadunandana's padas on Gaura and Gadadhara. The woman's words that she is "dying" express wonder and compassion at the sight of the Lord's ecstasy; there is no desire in the text. "He floats in that rasa" may refer either to Gadadhara Dasa or to the poet himself; GPT: a "lahu lahu" (light, soft) smile.

2. Yadunandana — "dāsa gadādhara badana heri…" (BR 12, p. 905)

Nagari-bhava. The second of Yadunandana's two "gitas" at the beginning of the cycle: Gaura, looking at the face of Dasa Gadadhara, signals to him with the corner of His eye, thrills, smiles; the woman saw Him on the bank of the Ganga — He steals the eyes of all young women. Raga kamoda.5

দাস গদাধর বদন হেরি ।
আঁখি-কোণে কহে ইঙ্গিত করি ॥

dāsa gadādhara badana heri |
ām̐khi-koṇe kahe iṅgita kari ||

dāsa gadādhara badana heri — looking at the face of Dasa Gadadhara; ām̐khi-koṇe kahe — He speaks with the corner of the eye; iṅgita kari — giving a sign

2.1Looking into the face of Dasa Gadadhara,
He speaks with the corner of His eye, giving a sign.6

কে জানে কি লাগি পুলকে তনু ।
হাসিতে অমিয়া বরিষে যনু ॥

ke jāne ki lāgi pulake tanu |
hāsite amiyā bariṣe yanu ||

ke jāne — who knows; ki lāgi — why; pulake tanu — the body thrills (bristles); hāsite — in His smile; amiyā bariṣe yanu — nectar seems to rain

2.2Who knows why His body thrills;
in His smile nectar seems to rain.

সুরনদী-তীরে দেখিলুঁ গোরা ।
অখিল তরুণী-নয়ন-চোরা ॥

suranadī-tīre dekhilum̐ gorā |
akhila taruṇī-nayana-corā ||

suranadī-tīre — on the bank of the Suranadi (Ganga); dekhilum̐ gorā — I saw Gora; akhila taruṇī-nayana-corā — the thief of the eyes of all young women

2.3On the bank of the Suranadi I saw Gora —
the thief of the eyes of all young women.

সহজ ভাঙর ভঙ্গিমা কাজে ।
পরাণে আজুলি কি আর লাজে ॥

sahaja bhāṅara bhaṅgimā kāje |
parāṇe ājuli ki āra lāje ||

sahaja — natural; bhāṅgara bhaṅgimā kāje — from the curve of the brows; parāṇe — while I live (in my heart); ājuli — little friend; ki āra lāje — what shame is left

2.4From the natural curve of His brows —
little friend, while I live, what shame is left?7

গ্রীবার ভঙ্গিমা কহিল নয় ।
আঁখি-পাখী পাখা পসারি রয় ॥

grībāra bhaṅgimā kahila naya |
ām̐khi-pākhī pākhā pasāri raya ||

grībāra bhaṅgimā — the curve of the neck; kahila naya — cannot be told; ām̐khi-pākhī — the bird of the eye; pākhā pasāri raya — stays with outspread wings

2.5The curve of His neck cannot be told:
the bird of the eye stays there, its wings outspread.

আজানুলম্বিত বাহুর শোভা ।
যুবতি-মরম যা হেরি লোভা ॥

ājānulambita bāhura śobhā |
yubati-marama yā heri lobhā ||

ājānulambita bāhura śobhā — the beauty of the arms reaching to the knees; yubati-marama — the hearts of young women; yā heri lobhā — crave, seeing it

2.6The beauty of His arms reaching to the knees —
seeing it, the hearts of young women crave.

অরুণ কমল-চরণতলে ।
যদু-মন রহু মধুপ-ছলে ॥

aruṇa kamala-caraṇatale |
yadu-mana rahu madhupa-chale ||

aruṇa kamala-caraṇa-tale — at the soles of the reddish lotus feet; yadu-mana — Yadu's mind; rahu — may abide; madhupa-chale — as a bee

2.7At the soles of His reddish lotus feet
may Yadu's mind abide as a bee.8

not in GPT1 or GPT2; in the catalogue — YN-005 (the second gita). Majumdar mentions both of Yadunandana's "gitas" at the beginning of the cycle as songs of a disciple of Gadadhara Dasa. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). Gadadhara Dasa in radha-bhava — chapter 11, no. 15). "Suranadi" (suranadī, "river of the gods") — the Ganga; so in the original. line can also be read: "in my heart, little friend, what shame is left?" — i.e., modesty is lost at the sight of Gaura. The nagari motif is rendered as in the original. the appendix).

3. Narahari — "taruṇī-parāṇa-corā gorārūpa…" (BR 12, pp. 905–906; GPT1 p. 171, no. 46)

Nagari-bhava. Gora's form steals the life of young women; blessed are those who drink it even once from the corner of the eye; Gaura, looking at Pandita Gadai, calls him "Radhika!", holds Dasa Gadadhara by the hand, thrills and smiles — the depth of this rasa cannot be reached; He walks the roads of Nadia, swaying like a nagara. Raga dhanashi. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada stands in the cycle of BR 12, in Vrajabuli.9

তরুণী-পরাণ-চোরা গোরারূপ, মাধুরী অমিয়া-ধারা ।
ধনি ধনি ধনি বারেক নয়ন-কোণেতে পিয়য়ে যারা ॥

taruṇī-parāṇa-corā gorārūpa, mādhurī amiyā-dhārā |
dhani dhani dhani bāreka nayana-koṇete piyaye yārā ||

taruṇī-parāṇa-corā — stealing the life of young women; gorārūpa — Gora's form; mādhurī — sweetness; amiyā-dhārā — a stream of nectar; dhani dhani dhani — blessed, blessed, blessed; bāreka — even once; nayana-koṇete — from the corner of the eye; piyaye yārā — they who drink

3.1Gora's form, which steals the life of young women — its sweetness is a stream of nectar; blessed, blessed, blessed are they who drink it even once from the corner of the eye!

সই, এ কথা কহিব কাকে ।
পণ্ডিত গদাই-পানে ঘন চাই রাধিকা বলিয়া ডাকে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

sai, e kathā kahiba kāke |
paṇḍita gadāi-pāne ghana cāi rādhikā baliyā ḍāke || dhru ||

sai — friend; e kathā kahiba kāke — to whom shall I tell this; paṇḍita gadāi-pāne — at Pandita Gadai; ghana cāi — gazing intently; rādhikā baliyā ḍāke — calls him "Radhika"

3.2(Refrain) Friend, to whom shall I tell this?
Gazing intently at Pandita Gadai, He calls him: "Radhika!"10

দাস গদাধর-করে দিয়া কর উলসে পুলক গা ।
মৃদু মৃদু হাসে, কিবা রসে ভাসে, কিছু না পাইলুঁ থা ॥

dāsa gadādhara-kare diyā kara ulase pulaka gā |
mṛdu mṛdu hāse, kibā rase bhāse, kichu nā pāilum̐ thā ||

dāsa gadādhara-kare — in the hand of Dasa Gadadhara; diyā kara — placing His hand; ulase — He rejoices; pulaka gā — His body bristling; mṛdu mṛdu hāse — smiles softly, softly; kibā rase bhāse — in what rasa He floats; kichu nā pāilum̐ thā — I found no bottom

3.3Placing His hand in the hand of Dasa Gadadhara, He thrills with joy, His body bristling; He smiles softly, softly — in what rasa does He float? I cannot reach the bottom.

নাগরালি-ঠাটে নদীয়ার বাটে হিলিতে দুলিতে যায় ।
নরহরি-মন-মোহন ভঙ্গিমা মদন মুরছে তায় ॥

nāgarāli-ṭhāṭe nadīyāra bāṭe hilite dulite yāya |
narahari-mana-mohana bhaṅgimā madana murache tāya ||

nāgarāli-ṭhāṭe — with a nagara's airs; nadīyāra bāṭe — along the roads of Nadia; hilite dulite yāya — goes swaying; narahari-mana-mohana bhaṅgimā — a pose enchanting Narahari's mind; madana murache tāya — Madana swoons at it

3.4With a nagara's airs He goes along the roads of Nadia, swaying;
His pose enchants Narahari's mind — Madana swoons at it.11

(dhanashi; scan PDF p. 430); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 46 (catalogue: NG-079). The pada stands third in the cycle of the speeches of the "anuragavatis", between two padas of Yadunandana, and, like all of Narahari Chakravarti's songs in BR, was written by him for this narrative (B). GPT1 readings: "mādhurī amiñā dhārā", "kichui nā pāi thā", "helite dulite". Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). His beloved in him. This is the Lord's own confidential mood, which the townswoman sees but does not understand ("to whom shall I tell?"). faithful to the author; the tradition does not accept the image of Gaura as nagara (introductory note, chapter 27): here it is the townswoman's view, while the Lord Himself is absorbed in Krishna's bhava for Radha (3.2–3.3). "Narahari's mind" — genitive of possession: the Lord's pose enchants the poet's mind.

4. Yadunandana — "sajani sai śuna gorā-aparūpa gāthā…" (BR 12, p. 906; GPT1 p. 169, no. 37)

Nagari-bhava. "Friend, listen to the wondrous song of Gora": the tale of the secret play with the young wives of Vraja has flooded the world; the fragrance of His body maddens the gods of love, the garland on His chest makes noble wives swoon; everything in Him is like the Moon of Gokula, only the colour is golden; now He calls "Radha!", now laughs, now weeps aloud. Raga karnatika.12

সজনি সই, শুন গোরা-অপরূপ গাথা ।
বরজ-বধূর সঙ্গে, বিলাস গোপন-রঙ্গে,
ভুবন ভাসিল সেই কথা ॥ ধ্রু ॥

sajani sai, śuna gorā-aparūpa gāthā |
baraja-badhūra saṅge, bilāsa gopana-raṅge,
bhubana bhāsila sei kathā || dhru ||

sajani sai — friend; śuna — listen; gorā-aparūpa gāthā — the wondrous song of Gora; baraja-badhūra saṅge — with the young wives of Vraja; bilāsa gopana-raṅge — secret play; bhubana bhāsila — has flooded the world; sei kathā — that tale

4.1(Refrain) Friend, listen to the wondrous song of Gora:
of the secret play with the young wives of Vraja —
that tale has flooded the world.13

অঙ্গের সৌরভে কত, মনমথ উনমত,
মধুকর-ছলে উড়ি ধায় ।
রঙ্গণ-ফুলের মালা, হিয়ার উপরে খেলা,
কুলবতী-মতি মুরছায় ॥

aṅgera saurabhe kata, manamatha unamata,
madhukara-chale uṛi dhāya |
raṅgaṇa-phulera mālā, hiyāra upare khelā,
kulabatī-mati murachāya ||

aṅgera saurabhe — from the fragrance of His body; kata manamatha unamata — how many Manmathas, maddened; madhukara-chale — in the guise of bees; uṛi dhāya — fly; raṅgaṇa-phulera mālā — the garland of rangana flowers; hiyāra upare khelā — plays upon His chest; kulabatī-mati murachāya — the minds of noble wives swoon

4.2From the fragrance of His body how many Manmathas, maddened,
fly to Him in the guise of bees;
the garland of rangana flowers plays upon His chest —
and the noble wives swoon.

গৌরবরণ দেখি, আর সব সেই সখি,
বলন গমন অঙ্গছটা ।
গোকুলচাঁদের ছাঁদ, পরতেকে ভুরু-ফাঁদ,
কুলবতী দুই কুলে কাঁটা ॥

gaurabaraṇa dekhi, āra saba sei sakhi,
balana gamana aṅgachaṭā |
gokulacām̐dera chām̐da, parateke bhuru-phām̐da,
kulabatī dui kule kām̐ṭā ||

gaurabaraṇa dekhi — I see the golden colour; āra saba sei — all else is the same; sakhi — friend; balana gamana aṅgachaṭā — speech, gait, radiance of the body; gokulacām̐dera chām̐da — the form of the Moon of Gokula; parateke — plainly; bhuru-phām̐da — the snare of the brows; kulabatī — to noble wives; dui kule kām̐ṭā — a thorn in both families

4.3I see the golden colour — and all else, friend, is the same:
the speech, the gait, the radiance of the body;
the form of the Moon of Gokula, the plain snare of the brows —
a thorn to noble wives in both their families.14

কে আছে এমন নারী, নয়ান-সন্ধান হেরি,
মুখচাঁদে হাসির মাধুরী ।
দেখিয়া ধৈরয ধরে, তবে সে যাইবে ঘরে,
মনমথে না করি বাউরী ॥

ke āche emana nārī, nayāna-sandhāna heri,
mukhacām̐de hāsira mādhurī |
dekhiyā dhairaya dhare, tabe se yāibe ghare,
manamathe nā kari bāurī ||

ke āche emana nārī — what woman is there; nayāna-sandhāna heri — seeing the aim of the eyes; mukhacām̐de hāsira mādhurī — the sweetness of the smile on the moon-face; dekhiyā dhairaya dhare — seeing it, keeps composure; tabe se yāibe ghare — then she will go home; manamathe nā kari bāurī — not made mad by Manmatha

4.4What woman, seeing the aim of His eyes
and the sweetness of the smile on His moon-face,
will keep her composure — and only then go home —
not driven mad by Manmatha?

খেনে রাধা বলি ডাকে, নয়ান মুদিয়া থাকে,
খেনে হাসে ভাবের আবেশে ।
খেনে কান্দে উভরায়, পুলকিত সর্বগায়,
এ যদুনন্দন ভালো বাসে ॥

khene rādhā bali ḍāke, nayāna mudiyā thāke,
khene hāse bhābera ābeśe |
khene kānde ubharāya, pulakita sarvagāya,
e yadunandana bhālo bāse ||

khene — now; rādhā bali ḍāke — calls "Radha"; nayāna mudiyā thāke — keeps His eyes closed; hāse bhābera ābeśe — laughs in the rapture of bhava; kānde ubharāya — weeps aloud; pulakita sarvagāya — His whole body bristling; e yadunandana bhālo bāse — this Yadunandana loves

4.5Now He calls "Radha!" and sits with His eyes closed,
now laughs, overwhelmed by bhava,
now weeps aloud, His whole body bristling —
this is what Yadunandana loves.15

(karnatika; scan PDF p. 428); GPT2 — sect. 3.2, no. 37 (catalogue: YN-003). Readings: GPT1 "āra saba sei śākhī", BR 1913 "sei sakhi" (noting the reading "sei sāthi"); BR 1960 "gorārūpa-gāthā". B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). townswoman (and the poet) recognizes in Gaura Krishna of Vraja Himself; cf. 4.3 "the form of the Moon of Gokula" and the endings of nos. 5–7 ("is He not the Moon of Gokula?"). ruin of one's good name in the father's and the husband's family; so the padas about Krishna speak of the gopis. The image is as in the original; Manmatha, the "god of love", is Kamadeva. The stanza turns from the townswomen to Gaura Himself: it is this bhava of His that the poet loves.

5. Yadunandana — "sai go nadīyā-jāhnabī-kūle…" (BR 12, p. 908; GPT1 p. 168, no. 36)

Nagari-bhava (praise of His form). "Friend, on the bank of the Jahnavi in Nadia — what creator fashioned that body from golden shirisha flowers?" His face a lotus, His lips bandhuli, His nose a kimshuka bud, His arms golden creepers; Gauranga cries "Hari!" and weeps on the lap of Dasa Gadadhara; is He not the Moon of Gokula? Raga mallarika.16

সই গো, নদীয়া-জাহ্নবী-কূলে ।

sthira haiyā punaḥ puche bāre bāre, tāhe nā uttara dila ||

20.8Seeing my immoderate weeping, she let go of her anger;
calming down, she asks again and again — I gave no answer.

খানিক থাকিয়া মনেতে বিচার করিয়া ধরিয়া করে ।
ধীরে ধীরে কহে, কিসের লাগিয়া না বোল মরম মোরে ॥

khānika thākiyā manete bicāra kariyā dhariyā kare |
dhīre dhīre kahe, kisera lāgiyā nā bola marama more ||

khānika thākiyā — after a little while; manete bicāra kariyā — thinking it over; dhariyā kare — taking my hand; dhīre dhīre kahe — says softly, softly; kisera lāgiyā — why; nā bola marama more — you do not tell me your heart

20.9After a little while, having thought it over, she took my hand
and says softly, softly: 'Why don't you open your heart to me?'

অনেক যতনে গদগদ ভাষে তা-সনে কহিনু কথা ।
মনের দুখেতে কান্দিয়া, এ সব কি লাগি পুছহ বৃথা ॥

aneka yatane gadagada bhāṣe tā-sane kahinu kathā |
manera dukhete kāndiyā, e saba ki lāgi puchaha bṛthā ||

aneka yatane — with great difficulty; gadagada bhāṣe — in a faltering voice; tā-sane kahinu kathā — I spoke to her; manera dukhete kāndiyā — weeping with grief in my heart; e saba ki lāgi — why all this; puchaha bṛthā — do you ask in vain

20.10With difficulty, in a faltering voice, I told her,
weeping, with grief in my heart: 'Why do you ask in vain?55

যা-সবারে তুমি প্রাণ-সম জান, সে করে দারুণ কাজ ।
ঘাটে মাঠে পথে নিন্দয়ে তোমারে, শুনিয়া পাইয়ে লাজ ॥

yā-sabāre tumi prāṇa-sama jāna, se kare dāruṇa kāja |
ghāṭe māṭhe pathe nindaye tomāre, śuniyā pāiye lāja ||

yā-sabāre tumi prāṇa-sama jāna — those whom you hold dear as life; se kare dāruṇa kāja — they do terrible things; ghāṭe māṭhe pathe — at the ghat, in the field, on the road; nindaye tomāre — they slander you; śuniyā pāiye lāja — I was ashamed to hear

20.11Those whom you hold dear as life do terrible things:
at the ghat, in the field, on the road they slander you — I was ashamed to hear it.

মনে করি, গলে কলসি বাঁধিয়া পশিব গঙ্গার জলে ।
তাহা না করিতে পারিয়ে, পাছে বা কলঙ্ক রটয়ে কুলে ॥

mane kari, gale kalasi bām̐dhiyā paśiba gaṅgāra jale |
tāhā nā karite pāriye, pāche bā kalaṅka raṭaye kule ||

mane kari — I thought; gale kalasi bām̐dhiyā — tying the pot to my neck; paśiba gaṅgāra jale — I would enter the Ganga; tāhā nā karite pāriye — I could not do it; pāche vā kalaṅka raṭaye kule — lest an ill name spread about the family

20.12I thought of tying the pot to my neck and throwing myself into the Ganga,
but could not — lest an ill name should spread about the family.

কি করিব আমি, তা-সবার সনে করিতে নারিয়ে দ্বন্দ্ব ।
যত অপযশ পাইল সে সব শুনিয়া হইনু ধন্দ ॥

ki kariba āmi, tā-sabāra sane karite nāriye dvandva |
yata apayaśa pāila se saba śuniyā hainu dhanda ||

ki kariba āmi — what could I do; tā-sabāra sane — with them; karite nāriye dvandva — I cannot quarrel; yata apayaśa pāila — all the ill repute you have got; se saba śuniyā — hearing it all; hainu dhanda — I was bewildered

20.13What could I do? I cannot quarrel with them;
all the ill they say of you — I heard it and was bewildered.

কাহারে করিব সাথী, সেথা কেহ না ছিল আমার সাথে ।
তা-সবার প্রতি কোরধ করিয়া কলসি ভাঙ্গিনু পথে ॥

kāhāre kariba sāthī, sethā keha nā chila āmāra sāthe |
tā-sabāra prati koradha kariyā kalasi bhāṅginu pathe ||

kāhāre kariba sāthī — whom could I make a witness; sethā keha nā chila āmāra sāthe — no one was with me there; tā-sabāra prati — at them; koradha kariyā — in anger; kalasi bhāṅginu pathe — I broke the pot on the road

20.14Whom could I call as a witness? No one was with me there;
in anger at them I broke the pot on the road.'

এত শুনি চিতে হরষিত অতি পীরিতি করিয়া মোরে ।
কত কত মতে বুঝাইয়া মুখ মুছিল আপন করে ॥

eta śuni cite haraṣita ati pīriti kariyā more |
kata kata mate bujhāiyā mukha muchila āpana kare ||

eta śuni — hearing this; cite haraṣita ati — greatly delighted at heart; pīriti kariyā more — caressing me; kata kata mate bujhāiyā — comforting me in every way; mukha muchila āpana kare — wiped my face with her own hand

20.15Hearing this, she was overjoyed, caressed me,
comforted me in every way and wiped my face with her own hand.

এইরূপে কালি বিষম সঙ্কট এড়ানু সাহস করি ।
নরহরি কহে, তুয়া চাতুরীর বালাই লইয়া মরি ॥

eirūpe kāli biṣama saṅkaṭa eṛānu sāhasa kari |
narahari kahe, tuyā cāturīra bālāi laiyā mari ||

eirūpe — thus; kāli — yesterday; biṣama saṅkaṭa eṛānu — I escaped a terrible fix; sāhasa kari — boldly; narahari kahe — Narahari says; tuyā cāturīra — of your cleverness; bālāi laiyā mari — I take upon myself the ills

কি কব সজনি ননদের কথা, কহিতে উপজে হাসি ।
তেঁহ পতিব্রতা, তার লেখে সব অসতী নদীয়াবাসী ॥

ki kaba sajani nanadera kathā, kahite upaje hāsi |
tem̐ha patibratā, tāra lekhe saba asatī nadīyābāsī ||

ki kaba sajani — what shall I say, friend; nanadera kathā — of my sister-in-law; kahite upaje hāsi — it is laughable to tell; teṃha patibratā — she is a faithful wife; tāra lekhe — by her reckoning; saba asatī nadīyābāsī — all the women of Nadia are unfaithful

21.1"What shall I say of my sister-in-law, friend? — it is laughable to tell:
she is a faithful wife, and all the women of Nadia, by her reckoning, are unfaithful.

আর বিপরীত, কারু সনে কথা কহিতে না দেয় মোরে ।
সতত তর্জন করে, একা কোথা যাইতে নারিয়ে ডরে ॥

āra biparīta, kāru sane kathā kahite nā deya more |
satata tarjana kare, ekā kothā yāite nāriye ḍare ||

āra biparīta — and worse; kāru sane kathā kahite — to speak with anyone; nā deya more — she does not let me; satata tarjana kare — she is forever scolding; ekā kothā yāite nāriye ḍare — I dare not go anywhere alone for fear

21.2And worse: she will not let me say a word to anyone,
she is forever scolding — I dare not go anywhere alone for fear.

মনোদুখে দিন রজনী মরিয়ে শুনিয়া নিন্দন-ভাষ ।
বিধি-প্রতি করি প্রার্থনা, ইহার দরপ হউক নাশ ॥

manodukhe dina rajanī mariye śuniyā nindana-bhāṣa |
bidhi-prati kari prārthanā, ihāra darapa hauka nāśa ||

manodukhe — with grief in my heart; dina rajanī mariye — day and night I was dying; śuniyā nindana-bhāṣa — hearing her abuse; bidhi-prati kari prārthanā — I prayed to the Creator; ihāra darapa hauka nāśa — let her pride be destroyed

21.3With grief in my heart, day and night, I was dying, hearing her abuse;
I prayed to the Creator: let her pride be destroyed.

না জানিয়ে কোন গুণে নিবেদন শুনিল সদয় বিধি ।
মনেতে করিনু যাহা, তাহা যেন তুরিতে হইল সিধি ॥

nā jāniye kona guṇe nibedana śunila sadaya bidhi |
manete karinu yāhā, tāhā yena turite haila sidhi ||

nā jāniye — I do not know; kona guṇe — for what merit; nibedana śunila — heard my plea; sadaya bidhi — the merciful Creator; manete karinu yāhā — what I had in mind; tāhā yena turite haila sidhi — that soon came true

21.4I do not know for what merit the merciful Creator heard my plea:
what I had in mind soon came true.

শুন গো সে কথা, গত দিন তেঁহ চলিলা কলসি লঞা ।
তার পাছে পাছে চলিনু মো পুনি তার অনুমতি পাঞা ॥

śuna go se kathā, gata dina tem̐ha calilā kalasi lañā |
tāra pāche pāche calinu mo puni tāra anumati pāñā ||

śuna go se kathā — listen to how it was; gata dina — yesterday; teṃha calilā kalasi lañā — she went, taking her pot; tāra pāche pāche calinu mo puni — and I followed behind her; tāra anumati pāñā — with her leave

21.5Listen to how it was: yesterday she went off, taking her pot;
and I followed behind her, with her leave.

সুরধুনী-ঘাট যাইতে আমরা দুজনে যাই যে পথে ।
সেই পথে গোরা দাঁড়াঞা আছেন প্রিয়-পারিষদ-সাথে ॥

suradhunī-ghāṭa yāite āmarā dujane yāi ye pathe |
sei pathe gorā dām̐ṛāñā āchena priya-pāriṣada-sāthe ||

suradhunī-ghāṭa yāite — going to the ghat of the Suradhuni; āmarā dujane yāi ye pathe — by the road we both go; sei pathe — on that road; gorā dām̐ṛāñā āchena — Gora is standing; priya-pāriṣada-sāthe — with His dear companions

21.6On the road by which we both go to the ghat of the Suradhuni,
on that very road Gora stands with His dear companions.

ও-রূপ-মাধুরী হেরিয়া ননদী ধৈরজ ধরিতে নারে ।
হইল বিষম থরহরি তনু, কাঁপয়ে মদন-ভরে ॥

o-rūpa-mādhurī heriyā nanadī dhairaja dharite nāre |
haila biṣama tharahari tanu, kām̐paye madana-bhare ||

o-rūpa-mādhurī heriyā — seeing the sweetness of that form; nanadī — my sister-in-law; dhairaja dharite nāre — cannot keep her composure; haila biṣama tharahari tanu — her body began to shake violently; kām̐paye madana-bhare — she trembles under Madana's onslaught

21.7Seeing the sweetness of that form, my sister-in-law could not keep her composure:
she began to shake all over, trembling under Madana's onslaught.58

কাঁখের কলস ভূমেতে পড়িল, আউলাইল মাথার কেশ ।
অঙ্গের বসন খসে অনায়াসে, স্মৃতির নাহিক লেশ ॥

kām̐khera kalasa bhūmete paṛila, āulāila māthāra keśa |
aṅgera basana khase anāyāse, smṛtira nāhika leśa ||

kām̐khera kalasa — the pot on her hip; bhūmete paṛila — fell to the ground; āulāila māthāra keśa — her hair came loose; aṅgera basana khase anāyāse — her clothes slip from her body of themselves; smṛtira nāhika leśa — there is not a trace of memory

21.8The pot fell from her hip to the ground, her hair came loose,
her clothes slip from her body of themselves — and there is not a trace of memory.

কতেক যতনে ধৈরজ ধরিল অধিক লজ্জিত হঞা ।
দুই করে ধরি ধীরে ধীরে কহে মোর মুখ-পানে চাঞা ॥

kateka yatane dhairaja dharila adhika lajjita hañā |
dui kare dhari dhīre dhīre kahe mora mukha-pāne cāñā ||

kateka yatane — with difficulty; dhairaja dharila — she regained her composure; adhika lajjita hañā — greatly embarrassed; dui kare dhari — taking both my hands; dhīre dhīre kahe — says softly, softly; mora mukha-pāne cāñā — looking into my face

21.9With difficulty she regained her composure, greatly embarrassed,
took me by both hands and says softly, softly, looking into my face:

নিশ্চয় জানিহ, গুণবতী বধূ, পরাণ-অধিক তুমি ।
কহিয়াছি কত, দোষ না লইবে, তোমার অধীন আমি ॥

niścaya jāniha, guṇabatī badhū, parāṇa-adhika tumi |
kahiyāchi kata, doṣa nā laibe, tomāra adhīna āmi ||

niścaya jāniha — know for certain; guṇabatī badhū — virtuous brother's wife; parāṇa-adhika tumi — you are dearer than life; kahiyāchi kata — all I have said; doṣa nā laibe — do not hold it against me; tomāra adhīna āmi — I am in your power

21.10'Know for certain: you, my virtuous brother's wife, are dearer to me than life;
all I have said to you — do not hold it against me; I am in your power.

যখন যে কাজ কর, তাহা মোরে কবে নিঃসঙ্কোচ হঞা ।
প্রাণধন দিয়া সহায় করিব, বলয়ে শপথ খাঞা ॥

yakhana ye kāja kara, tāhā more kabe niḥsaṅkoca hañā |
prāṇadhana diyā sahāya kariba, balaye śapatha khāñā ||

yakhana ye kāja kara — whatever you do; tāhā more kabe — tell me; niḥsaṅkoca hañā — without embarrassment; prāṇadhana diyā — even at the cost of my life; sahāya kariba — I will help; balaye śapatha khāñā — she says, swearing

21.11Whatever you do — tell me without embarrassment;
I will help you, even at the cost of my life,' she swears.

আনে না কহিও সে সব কাহিনী, রাখিহ গোপন করি ।
ঠেকিনু এ রসে, কি কব, পাগলী করিলে গৌরহরি ॥

āne nā kahio se saba kāhinī, rākhiha gopana kari |
ṭhekinu e rase, ki kaba, pāgalī karile gaurahari ||

āne nā kahio — tell no one; se saba kāhinī — all this; rākhiha gopana kari — keep it secret; ṭhekinu e rase — I have fallen into this rasa; ki kaba — what can I say; pāgalī karile gaurahari — Gaurahari has driven me mad

21.12'Only tell no one about this, keep it secret;
I have fallen into this rasa — what can I say? — Gaurahari has driven me mad!'

এইরূপ বহু কহিল, শুনিয়া বাড়িল অশেষ সুখ ।
পুরবের কথা বিচার করিতে উঠিল অনেক দুখ ॥

eirūpa bahu kahila, śuniyā bāṛila aśeṣa sukha |
purabera kathā bicāra karite uṭhila aneka dukha ||

eirūpa bahu kahila — thus she said much; śuniyā bāṛila aśeṣa sukha — hearing it, my joy grew endlessly; purabera kathā bicāra karite — recalling what had gone before; uṭhila aneka dukha — much bitterness rose

21.13Thus she said much — hearing it, my joy knew no bounds,
and remembering what had gone before, much bitterness rose in me.

মনেতে হইল, এ সকল কথা বেকত করিলে কাজ ।
নরহরি কহে, সাধু-রীতি যার, সে রাখে পরের লাজ ॥

manete haila, e sakala kathā bekata karile kāja |
narahari kahe, sādhu-rīti yāra, se rākhe parera lāja ||

manete haila — I thought; e sakala kathā — all this; bekata karile kāja — what use in revealing; narahari kahe — Narahari says; sādhu-rīti yāra — one whose ways are noble; se rākhe parera lāja — guards another's shame

21.14I thought: what is the use of spreading all this?"

Summary of chapter 29

The chapter opens the nagari padas signed "Narahari" from section 3.2 of GPT. Before translating, section 3.2 of GPT1 (pp. 157–237, 180 padas) was read through on the scan: 95 padas bear Narahari's signature, of which 32 were not in the catalogue (new lines NG-334…365); the witness of almost all the long padas of this series is Narahari Chakravarti's *Gaura-charita-chintamani, kiranas 7–11 ("the nagaris of Navadvipa"), which confirms Majumdar's argument: the long padas of GPT with this signature are not Sarakara's. Translated: the cycle of the Bhakti-ratnakara (12th wave) — the speeches of the "anuragavatis", the women of Nadia, by the tree on the bank of the Ganga (nos. 1–7: five padas of Yadunandana, a pada of Yadu and a pada of Narahari Chakravarti; in them the townswomen see Gaura in the bhava of Krishna calling Radha and recognize in Him "the Moon of Gokula"); the short padas of GPT1 3.2 nos. 39–45 in simple Bengali, which the GPT2 index assigns to Sarakara (nos. 8–13; "probably Sarakara" — C, no. 43 — "not established"); the beginning of the 7th kirana of GCC — the townswomen's morning conversations and their stories of how, deceiving their elders, they saw Gaura (nos. 14–21; "probably Chakravarti" — B). The padas of other poets of the section (nos. 49–60, Govinda Dasa, Jnanadasa) were not translated; Lochana Dasa's padas (nos. 61–85, 116) are translated in chapters 28 and 34.*
